steps.message:
## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

class Panel(JupyterMixin):
    """A console renderable that draws a border around its contents.

    Example:
        >>> console.print(Panel("Hello, World!"))

    Args:
        renderable (RenderableType): A console renderable object.
        box (Box): A Box instance that defines the look of the border (see :ref:`appendix_box`. Defaults to box.ROUNDED.
        title (Optional[TextType], optional): Optional title displayed in panel header. Defaults to None.
        title_align (AlignMethod, optional): Alignment of title. Defaults to "center".
        subtitle (Optional[TextType], optional): Optional subtitle displayed in panel footer. Defaults to None.
        subtitle_align (AlignMethod, optional): Alignment of subtitle. Defaults to "center".
        safe_box (bool, optional): Disable box characters that don't display on windows legacy terminal with *raster* fonts. Defaults to True.
        expand (bool, optional): If True the panel will stretch to fill the console width, otherwise it will be sized to fit the contents. Defaults to True.
        style (str, optional): The style of the panel (border and contents). Defaults to "none".
        border_style (str, optional): The style of the border. Defaults to "none".
        width (Optional[int], optional): Optional width of panel. Defaults to None to auto-detect.
        height (Optional[int], optional): Optional height of panel. Defaults to None to auto-detect.
        padding (Optional[PaddingDimensions]): Optional padding around renderable. Defaults to 0.
        highlight (bool, optional): Enable automatic highlighting of panel title (if str). Defaults to False.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        renderable: "RenderableType",
        box: Box = ROUNDED,
        *,
        title: Optional[TextType] = None,
        title_align: AlignMethod = "center",
        subtitle: Optional[TextType] = None,
        subtitle_align: AlignMethod = "center",
        safe_box: Optional[bool] = None,
        expand: bool = True,
        style: StyleType = "none",
        border_style: StyleType = "none",
        width: Optional[int] = None,
        height: Optional[int] = None,
        padding: PaddingDimensions = (0, 1),
        highlight: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self.renderable = renderable
        self.box = box
        self.title = title
        self.title_align: AlignMethod = title_align
        self.subtitle = subtitle
        self.subtitle_align = subtitle_align
        self.safe_box = safe_box
        self.expand = expand
        self.style = style
        self.border_style = border_style
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.padding = padding
        self.highlight = highlight

    @classmethod
    def fit(
        cls,
        renderable: "RenderableType",
        box: Box = ROUNDED,
        *,
        title: Optional[TextType] = None,
        title_align: AlignMethod = "center",
        subtitle: Optional[TextType] = None,
        subtitle_align: AlignMethod = "center",
        safe_box: Optional[bool] = None,
        style: StyleType = "none",
        border_style: StyleType = "none",
        width: Optional[int] = None,
        height: Optional[int] = None,
        padding: PaddingDimensions = (0, 1),
        highlight: bool = False,
    ) -> "Panel":
        """An alternative constructor that sets expand=False."""
        return cls(
            renderable,
            box,
            title=title,
            title_align=title_align,
            subtitle=subtitle,
            subtitle_align=subtitle_align,
            safe_box=safe_box,
            style=style,
            border_style=border_style,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            padding=padding,
            highlight=highlight,
            expand=False,
        )

from rich.console import Console
from rich.panel import Panel
import io

def test_panel_title_background():
    console = Console(
        file=io.StringIO(),
        width=50,
        height=20,
        legacy_windows=False,
        force_terminal=True,
        color_system="truecolor",
    )
    panel = Panel("Content", title="Title", style="on blue")
    console.print(panel)
    result = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(result))
    # Check if the background style is present in the title area
    # 'on blue' is \x1b[44m
    if "\x1b[44m" not in result:
        print("FAILURE: Background style not found in output")
    else:
        print("SUCCESS: Background style found in output")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_panel_title_background()

echo 'from rich.console import Console
from rich.panel import Panel
import io

def test_panel_title_background():
    console = Console(
        file=io.StringIO(),
        width=50,
        height=20,
        legacy_windows=False,
        force_terminal=True,
        color_system="truecolor",
    )
    panel = Panel("Content", title="Title", style="on blue")
    console.print(panel)
    result = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(result))
    
    # The title " Title " should be preceded by the background style.
    # In the output: ...\x1b[0m Title \x1b[44m...
    # It should be: ...\x1b[44m Title \x1b[0m... or similar.
    
    # Let's look for " Title " and see what's before it.
    title_text = " Title "
    idx = result.find(title_text)
    if idx == -1:
        print("FAILURE: Title text not found")
        return
    
    before = result[max(0, idx-10):idx]
    after = result[idx+len(title_text):idx+len(title_text)+10]
    print(f"Before: {repr(before)}")
    print(f"After: {repr(after)}")
    
    if "\x1b[44m" not in before:
        print("FAILURE: Background style not found before title")
    else:
        print("SUCCESS: Background style found before title")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_panel_title_background()' > /tmp/repro.py
